metadata.title: Amsterdam Tree Governance Explorer
metadata.scope: Municipal management of public trees in Amsterdam; interpretive research model.
metadata.schema: Typed property graph. Nodes = actors, processes, data/objects, rules and ecological objects. Edges = typed relations with provenance, basis and confidence.
metadata.caveat: This is a research synthesis, not an official City of Amsterdam organization chart. Some relations are explicit in sources; others are marked as synthesis.
metadata.verification: Every node and relation was desk-reviewed against current Amsterdam municipal/regulatory sources; synthesis relations remain interpretive.

nodes.label: College of Mayor & Alderpersons
nodes.summary: Amsterdam's municipal executive. It exercises executive and delegated powers in tree governance, including powers assigned to the college in the Bomenverordening and implementation of adopted policy.
nodes.why: Separates executive municipal authority from the Municipal Council, which adopts ordinances and strategic frameworks.

nodes.label: V&OR
nodes.summary: Verkeer & Openbare Ruimte (V&OR): owner/source holder of the municipal tree dataset and an important policy/asset-management actor in public-space standards.
nodes.why: Important bridge between policy, public-space design and asset information.

nodes.label: Stadswerken / GFF
nodes.summary: Operational public-space organization. Within Stadswerken, Groen, Flora en Fauna is responsible for daily management and maintenance of parks and tree/green assets in public space.
nodes.why: Core operational manager of public greenery.

nodes.label: Team Bomen
nodes.summary: Specialist tree team within Groen, Flora en Fauna. Current municipal recruitment material states that it manages trees in Centrum and some monumental trees elsewhere, and works with specialist contracts, inspections, felling/replanting procedures and emergency services.
nodes.why: Represents specialist arboricultural expertise inside the municipal management system.

nodes.label: City ecologists
nodes.summary: Ecological specialists who advise projects on biodiversity and ecological design choices.
nodes.why: Connects biodiversity knowledge to public-space projects and tree decisions.

nodes.label: District permit teams & daily boards
nodes.summary: For most tree-permit applications, postcode routes the application to the relevant district permit department and the district daily board takes the decision. Some metropolitan areas are handled by ODNZKG.
nodes.why: Represents the normal district-level administrative and decision route for tree permits while making the ODNZKG exception explicit.

nodes.label: Public-space project teams
nodes.summary: Teams responsible for redesign, infrastructure renewal and other projects that can affect existing trees.
nodes.why: Major source of tree-management decisions outside routine maintenance.

nodes.label: Tree contractors
nodes.summary: External contractors carry out parts of establishment care and specialist tree work under municipal contracts.
nodes.why: Key implementation actor between municipal instructions and physical tree care.

nodes.label: Residents & local groups
nodes.summary: Observe trees, submit public-space reports, participate in selected planning processes and can object to felling permits.
nodes.why: The principal public interface to the formal tree-management system.

nodes.label: Tree nurseries
nodes.summary: Supply planting stock selected for Amsterdam projects.
nodes.why: Upstream actor in the physical tree lifecycle.

nodes.label: Green & spatial strategic frameworks
nodes.summary: A synthesis node grouping long-term citywide green and spatial goals that influence tree policy and public-space management.
nodes.why: Represents the strategic policy layer rather than one single policy document.

nodes.label: Puccini + Handboek Groen
nodes.summary: Amsterdam's public-space design standard. The policy framework and Handboek Groen translate city policy into design and technical requirements for green infrastructure, including trees and growing places.
nodes.why: Translates strategic goals into design constraints and repeatable technical choices.

nodes.label: Bomenverordening 2014
nodes.summary: Amsterdam's current municipal tree ordinance. It regulates felling and major tree interventions, sets refusal grounds, provides for replanting/financial compensation, protected-tree rules and possible Tree Effect Analysis requirements.
nodes.why: Formal citywide legal basis for the local tree-permit and replanting regime.

nodes.label: Biodiversity policy / Plan 2025–2030
nodes.summary: Amsterdam biodiversity policy, including the 2025–2030 plan for the ecological structure and parks. It links ecological quality requirements to management contracts and monitoring; its formal action-plan scope is narrower than all street-tree management.
nodes.why: Introduces ecological objectives and management/monitoring requirements while preserving the plan's actual scope.

nodes.label: Translate policy to management
nodes.summary: Converts strategic political and ecological goals into management standards, programmes and operational priorities.
nodes.why: Abstract synthesis node used to connect policy documents to implementation.

nodes.label: Plan public-space project
nodes.summary: Design or redesign streets, squares, quays and other public spaces where existing or future trees are part of the project.
nodes.why: Project route can create opportunities for new planting or pressures on existing trees.

nodes.label: Tree Effect Analysis (BEA)
nodes.summary: A Tree Effect Analysis evaluates tree condition/value and likely effects of proposed works. Amsterdam may require one where works threaten the sustainable preservation of a protected tree, and major municipal projects also use BEAs as decision support.
nodes.why: Structured interface between infrastructure projects and tree expertise.
nodes.translation: BEA = Boom Effect Analyse / Tree Effect Analysis

nodes.label: Select species & design site
nodes.summary: Selects tree/species and designs the growing place within public-space standards and site constraints.
nodes.why: Critical upstream determinant of long-term tree condition and ecological value.

nodes.label: Plant tree
nodes.summary: Physical installation of the selected tree in its prepared growing place.
nodes.why: Transition from project/design system into the managed tree asset lifecycle.

nodes.label: Establishment care (0-4 yrs)
nodes.summary: Early-life care of newly planted trees; Amsterdam states that a contractor provides care during the first four years.
nodes.why: Distinct responsibility phase before routine municipal management.

nodes.label: Routine inspection
nodes.summary: Routine safety/condition inspection of managed street and avenue trees. Amsterdam states that roughly 300,000 such trees are checked at least every three years, with older/monumental trees checked more often.
nodes.why: Main monitoring loop that turns physical tree state into actionable information.

nodes.label: Handle citizen report
nodes.summary: Receives and evaluates a resident report or question about a specific public tree.
nodes.why: Alternative observation pathway into the management system.

nodes.label: Assess condition & options
nodes.summary: Interprets inspection, asset, project and—where relevant—ecological/legal information to identify options such as retention, maintenance, growing-place improvement, transplanting or removal.
nodes.why: Decision-preparation stage where multiple information streams converge.

nodes.label: Prune / maintain / improve site
nodes.summary: Routine or corrective tree care, pruning and growing-place work. Municipal data records measures, urgency/planning and executing organizations; Stadswerken/GFF has daily tree-and-green maintenance responsibility.
nodes.why: Primary non-removal intervention in the lifecycle.

nodes.label: Management decision
nodes.summary: Analytical decision point representing selection of a management course: retain, maintain, improve growing place, transplant, fell/replace or move into a permit/project route.
nodes.why: This is a synthesis node joining documented information and formal routes; it is not the name of one official Amsterdam procedure.

nodes.label: Felling / pruning permit process
nodes.summary: Formal omgevingsvergunning route for felling, transplanting and qualifying major pruning. Most applications are processed through district permit teams/daily boards with municipal tree-expert advice; designated metropolitan areas are handled by ODNZKG.
nodes.why: Legal authorization layer between decision and many major interventions.

nodes.label: Fell / transplant / emergency work
nodes.summary: Physical major intervention, including felling, transplanting or urgent safety/disease response.
nodes.why: High-impact branch of the tree lifecycle.

nodes.label: Replant / compensate
nodes.summary: Replacement or compensation following felling. The ordinance normally attaches a replant obligation; Amsterdam's current compensation policy seeks equivalent replacement, with financial compensation to the municipal replant fund where physical replacement is not possible.
nodes.why: Closes the formal replacement loop after felling.

nodes.label: Monitor green outcomes
nodes.summary: Monitoring of green/ecological outcomes. The Plan Biodiversiteit requires recurring ecological monitoring/inspection in ecological core and connection zones, while Monitor Groen tracks broader city-level green indicators such as canopy cover.
nodes.why: Connects tree management back to wider ecological and policy outcomes.

nodes.label: Tree passport / GISIB record
nodes.summary: Structured record for a managed tree; published through the Bomenkaart and underlying municipal data services.
nodes.why: Persistent digital representation linking tree identity, condition and management history.

nodes.label: Inspection record
nodes.summary: Recorded result of a tree safety/condition inspection, linked to the managed tree in Amsterdam's GISIB-based data model.
nodes.why: Evidence object used in management decisions and asset history.

nodes.label: Maintenance task
nodes.summary: Recorded management measure/work item for a tree, including manager decision, detailed measure, urgency/planning and executing organization where recorded.
nodes.why: Links assessment and planning to field execution.

nodes.label: Citizen report / question
nodes.summary: Resident-submitted observation, concern or question about a specific public tree.
nodes.why: Publicly generated information entering the operational system.

nodes.label: BEA report
nodes.summary: Tree Effect Analysis output documenting condition, value, project effects and options.
nodes.why: Formal evidence object in project-related tree decisions.

nodes.label: Permit decision / conditions
nodes.summary: Formal permit outcome and conditions, including possible replanting or financial-compensation requirements.
nodes.why: Legal object authorizing or restricting major tree intervention.

nodes.label: Bomenboekhouding
nodes.summary: Public Bomenboekhouding reporting permit applications and decisions, number of trees permitted/refused, imposed replant and replant-fund amounts. It should not be read as a complete real-time record of completed replacement planting.
nodes.why: Transparency / accountability output across the permit and replanting system.

nodes.label: Managed public tree stock
nodes.summary: The physical stock of roughly 300,000 municipality-managed public trees represented in Amsterdam's tree-management and asset-information systems.
nodes.why: The central physical object around which the governance network is organized.

nodes.label: Biodiversity & ecosystem services
nodes.summary: Ecological and public values associated with urban trees, including habitat/connectivity, shade/cooling, water regulation and other ecosystem services.
nodes.why: Represents outcomes that tree management is intended to protect or increase.

nodes.label: Municipal Council
nodes.summary: Amsterdam's elected municipal council. It adopts municipal ordinances and citywide strategic frameworks that shape tree governance.
nodes.why: The earlier prototype incorrectly combined the Council and College into one actor; they have distinct formal roles.

nodes.label: Municipal tree expert
nodes.summary: A municipal boomdeskundige advises on every tree-felling permit application and may recommend refusal or an alternative that retains the tree.
nodes.why: The current permit route explicitly requires specialist tree advice; this role was missing from the prototype.

nodes.label: ODNZKG
nodes.summary: Omgevingsdienst Noordzeekanaalgebied handles tree-felling permit applications in designated metropolitan areas such as Zuidas and Havengebied.
nodes.why: Makes the documented exception to the normal district permit route visible.
nodes.translation: North Sea Canal Area Environment Agency

edges.label: can trigger / require BEA when relevant
adopted municipal ordinance
edges.evidence: The regulation metadata identifies the gemeenteraad as adopting authority.

edges.label: directs executive implementation
edges.evidence: Abstract implementation link; the college holds multiple executive powers but this node is not a single formal procedure.

edges.label: advises on every felling application
edges.evidence: Q2 2026 Bomenboekhouding states every application is assessed by a municipal tree expert.

edges.label: handles designated metropolitan-area applications
edges.evidence: Q2 2026 Bomenboekhouding names Zuidas and Havengebied as examples.

edges.label: sets ecological management KPIs in parks / ecological structure
edges.evidence: Plan Biodiversiteit 2025–2030 puts ecological quality requirements into ecological green-management contracts.

edges.label: assigns executive powers
edges.evidence: The ordinance assigns multiple powers to the college of mayor and alderpersons.
